record.context_brief: Replace IID by stationary ergodic in one-dimensional criterion
record.original_question: Consider the one-dimensional recurrence/transience criterion for excited random walks under the assumptions that the family of cookie stacks is i.i.d., that there is a deterministic bound M with M(z) <= M almost surely for every site z (so each site has only boundedly many non-placebo cookies), and that every direction remains possible at every site and visit in the weak-ellipticity sense. Can the i.i.d. assumption on the cookie stacks be weakened to the stationary-and-ergodic assumption while keeping the same recurrence/transience conclusion?

evidence.quote: (IID)              the family (ω(z, ·, ·))z∈Zd of cookie stacks is i.i.d. under P.
(SE)                    the family (ω(z, ·, ·))z∈Zd is under P stationary and ergodic with respect to the shifts on Zd.
(WEL)             For all z ∈ Zd, e ∈ E: P [∀i ∈ N : ω(z, e, i) > 0] > 0.
(BD)     there is a deterministic M ∈ N such that for all z ∈ Zd : P-a.s. M (z) ≤ M .
(3.10)                           (IID), (BD), and (WEL). Then the ERW is recurrent if δ ∈ [−1, 1], transient to the right if δ > 1 and transient to the left if δ < −1.
Problem 3.11. Can one replace in (3.10) the assumption (IID) by (SE)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix the lattice $\mathbb{Z}$ and let $E=\{+1,-1\}$. A cookie environment is a family $\omega=(\omega(z,\cdot,\cdot))_{z\in\mathbb{Z}}$ where, for each site $z\in\mathbb{Z}$ and each integer $i\geq 1$, the pair $(\omega(z,+1,i),\omega(z,-1,i))$ is a probability vector on $E$ (i.e. $\omega(z,+1,i),\omega(z,-1,i)\geq 0$ and $\omega(z,+1,i)+\omega(z,-1,i)=1$). The pair indexed by $i$ is called the $i$-th cookie at site $z$. Given $\omega$, the excited random walk $(X_n)_{n\geq 0}$ started at $0$ is the nearest-neighbor process on $\mathbb{Z}$ such that, conditionally on the past, when the walk is at site $z$ for the $i$-th time it jumps to $z+e$ with probability $\omega(z,e,i)$. A cookie at $(z,i)$ is called a placebo if $\omega(z,+1,i)=\omega(z,-1,i)=1/2$, and we set
$$M(z)=\inf\{i\geq 1:\omega(z,\cdot,j)\text{ is a placebo for all }j\geq i\}-1,$$
the number of non-placebo cookies at $z$.

Assumptions. Let $P$ denote the law of $\omega$. Assume:
(BD) there exists a deterministic constant $M\in\mathbb{N}$ with $M(z)\leq M$ for all $z\in\mathbb{Z}$, $P$-a.s.;
(WEL) for every $z\in\mathbb{Z}$ and every $e\in\{+1,-1\}$, $P[\omega(z,e,i)>0\text{ for all }i\geq 1]>0$;
(SE) the family $(\omega(z,\cdot,\cdot))_{z\in\mathbb{Z}}$ is stationary and ergodic under $P$ with respect to the shifts on $\mathbb{Z}$.

Known result (i.i.d. case). When (SE) is strengthened to the assumption (IID) that $(\omega(z,\cdot,\cdot))_{z\in\mathbb{Z}}$ is i.i.d. under $P$, there is a sharp recurrence/transience criterion for $(X_n)$ in terms of the expected total drift $\delta=E\big[\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}(2\omega(0,+1,i)-1)\big]$: the walk is recurrent iff $|\delta|\leq 1$ and is transient to $\pm\infty$ if $\pm\delta>1$.

Question. Under assumptions (BD), (WEL), and (SE), does the same recurrence/transience criterion (with the same threshold in terms of the expected total drift per site) hold for $(X_n)$? In other words, can the i.i.d. assumption on the cookie environment be weakened to stationarity and ergodicity without changing the recurrence/transience conclusion?
artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate that for one-dimensional excited random walks with stationary ergodic cookie environments, the recurrence/transience threshold is known to extend from the i.i.d. case when all cookies are positive (even for unbounded stacks), but extending the threshold to general stationary ergodic environments where cookies may be negative—even with bounded stacks—is reported as unknown. No source found establishing the full equivalence under (BD)+(WEL)+(SE), so the question appears still open.

status_evidence.title: One-Dimensional Excited Random Walk with Unboundedly Many Cookies (CUNY thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: If all cookies are positive then the same threshold for transience vs. recurrence holds, even if the cookie stacks are unbounded. However, it is unknown if the threshold for transience vs. recurrence extends to the case when cookies may be negative (even for bounded stacks).
status_evidence.claim: The extension of the recurrence/transience threshold to stationary ergodic environments with possibly negative cookies is reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Multi-excited random walks on integers (Zerner)
status_evidence.snippet: Transient and recurrent regimes in one-dimension were characterized by Zerner for stationary and ergodic environments under additional assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial stationary-ergodic results exist (e.g., for nonnegative cookies) but do not cover the general bounded weakly-elliptic case.
